ex: {Jag vet inte} om jag hinner.
exEn: I don't know if I'll have time.
note: veta = to know a fact; to know a person is känna. Casually just: Vet inte.

ex: – Vem vann matchen? – {Ingen aning}, jag såg den inte.
exEn: – Who won the game? – No idea, I didn't see it.
note: aning = hunch, notion. Full sentence: Jag har ingen aning.

ex: – Kan du hämta mig vid stationen? – {Inga problem}!
exEn: – Can you pick me up at the station? – No problem!
note: problem is the same in the plural: ett problem, två problem.

ex: – Förlåt att jag är sen! – {Ingen fara}, vi har inte börjat än.
exEn: – Sorry I'm late! – No worries, we haven't started yet.
note: Literally 'no danger'. A kind reply to an apology.

ex: – Ska jag hjälpa dig? – Nej tack, {det är lugnt}.
exEn: – Shall I help you? – No thanks, it's fine.
note: Literally 'it's calm'. A relaxed reply to thanks, apologies and offers.

ex: – Jag glömde din bok. – {Det gör inget}, ta med den imorgon.
exEn: – I forgot your book. – It doesn't matter, bring it tomorrow.
note: Also: Det gör inget om du är sen (It's OK if you're late).

ex: {Det spelar ingen roll} vad andra tycker.
exEn: It doesn't matter what other people think.
note: Literally 'it plays no role'. Spelar det någon roll? = Does it matter?

en: it's not the end of the world
alt: not the end of the world
ex: Vi förlorade, men {det är inte hela världen}.
exEn: We lost, but it's not the end of the world.
note: Literally 'it's not the whole world'.

ex: – Jag mår mycket bättre nu. – {Vad bra}!
exEn: – I feel much better now. – That's good!
note: vad + adjective in the ett-form = how …!: Vad skönt! (What a relief!), Vad gulligt! (How cute!)

ex: – Vi ska gifta oss! – Åh, {vad roligt}!
exEn: – We're getting married! – Oh, how lovely!
note: Said when you hear good news. Vad kul! means the same and is just as common. The g in roligt is silent.

ex: – Jag kan inte komma på festen. – {Vad synd}!
exEn: – I can't come to the party. – What a shame!
note: synd also means 'sin'. Det är synd om honom = I feel sorry for him.

ex: – Jag fixar biljetterna. – {Toppen}, tack!
exEn: – I'll sort out the tickets. – Great, thanks!
note: Literally 'the top'. Also: Det var toppen! (It was great!)

ex: {Oj}, förlåt! Det var inte meningen.
exEn: Oops, sorry! I didn't mean to.
note: Shows surprise or a small mistake. Oj då! = Oops! / Oh dear!

ex: {Usch}, vad kallt det är idag!
exEn: Ugh, it's so cold today!
note: Shows dislike or disgust: Usch, vad äckligt! (Yuck, how gross!)

ex: – Jag ska flytta till Norge. – {Jaså}? När då?
exEn: – I'm moving to Norway. – Really? When?
note: Shows surprise or interest in news. Pronounced 'jasså'.

ex: {Va}? Har du sålt bilen?
exEn: What? You've sold the car?
note: Casual. More polite: Förlåt? or Vad sa du? Also a tag at the end: Snyggt, va? (Nice, huh?)

ex: – Filmen var för lång. – Ja, {jag håller med}.
exEn: – The movie was too long. – Yes, I agree.
note: From hålla med (to agree), with stress on med. Jag håller med dig = I agree with you.

ex: – Bor du i Uppsala? – Ja, {det stämmer}.
exEn: – Do you live in Uppsala? – Yes, that's right.
note: stämma = to be correct, to add up. Stämmer det? = Is that right?

ex: – Så vi ses klockan sex? – {Precis}!
exEn: – So we'll meet at six? – Exactly!
note: As an adverb it also means 'just': precis som jag (just like me), Jag kom precis hem (I just got home).

ex: – Får jag låna din cykel? – {Absolut}!
exEn: – Can I borrow your bike? – Absolutely!
note: Absolut inte! = Absolutely not! / No way!

ex: – Får jag sitta här? – {Ja visst}!
exEn: – May I sit here? – Sure!
note: visst also asks for agreement: Visst är det fint här? (Isn't it lovely here?)

ex: Hon vann {så klart}, som vanligt.
exEn: She won, of course, as usual.
note: Also written såklart. Självklart means the same.

ex: – Ska vi ses vid sju? – {Det låter bra}!
exEn: – Shall we meet at seven? – Sounds good!
note: låta = to sound. Det låter kul! = Sounds fun!

ex: Det är kallt idag, {eller hur}?
exEn: It's cold today, isn't it?
note: Like English isn't it? or don't you?, but it never changes form.

ex: – Kommer du imorgon? – {Det beror på} vädret.
exEn: – Are you coming tomorrow? – It depends on the weather.
note: bero på = to depend on; also 'to be due to': Förseningen beror på snön (The delay is due to the snow).

ex: – Har du ätit? – Nej, {inte än}.
exEn: – Have you eaten? – No, not yet.
note: In a full sentence än usually comes last: Jag har inte ätit än. Also: inte ännu.

ex: Vi kan äta något enkelt, {typ} pasta.
exEn: We can eat something simple, like pasta.
note: Very common in casual speech (Det tar typ en timme = It takes about an hour). Avoid it in formal writing.

ex: Det var {liksom} lite konstigt.
exEn: It was, like, a bit weird.
note: A filler word in casual speech. In formal Swedish it means 'like; as': liksom förra året (as last year).

ex: {Hur som helst}, nu måste jag gå.
exEn: Anyway, I have to go now.
note: Also 'any old way': Man kan inte parkera hur som helst (You can't park any old way).

ex: Det regnade, men vi hade kul {i alla fall}.
exEn: It rained, but we had fun anyway.
note: Also 'at least': Det var i alla fall gratis (At least it was free). In texts often iaf.

ex: {Grattis} på födelsedagen!
exEn: Happy birthday!
note: Short for gratulerar. Used for birthdays, new jobs, passed exams and so on.

ex: {Lycka till} med provet imorgon!
exEn: Good luck with the test tomorrow!
note: lycka means both luck and happiness.

ex: Jag hörde att du är sjuk. {Krya på dig}!
exEn: I heard you're sick. Get well soon!
note: From krya på sig (to get better). To several people: Krya på er!

ex: {Bra jobbat}, allihop! Nu är vi klara.
exEn: Well done, everyone! We're finished now.
note: jobbat is the supine of jobba (to work). Also common: Snyggt jobbat!

ex: Här är ditt kvitto. {Ha en bra dag}!
exEn: Here's your receipt. Have a nice day!
note: Typical reply: Tack, detsamma! (Thanks, you too!)

ex: Ska ni till Paris? {Ha det så kul}!
exEn: Are you going to Paris? Have fun!
note: Also: Ha så kul! or Ha det så roligt!

ex: God natt, älskling. {Sov gott}!
exEn: Good night, darling. Sleep well!
note: sov is the imperative of sova (to sleep); gott here means 'well'.

ex: – Trevlig helg! – Tack, {detsamma}!
exEn: – Have a nice weekend! – Thanks, you too!
note: The usual reply to good wishes like Trevlig helg! or Ha en bra dag!, often as Tack, detsamma!

ex: Barn, glöm inte att säga {tack för maten}!
exEn: Kids, don't forget to say thank you for the meal!
note: Said to the host, or whoever cooked, when you get up from the table.

ex: {Tack för senast}! Det var en jättetrevlig kväll.
exEn: Thanks for the other night! It was a really lovely evening.
note: Said the next time you see someone you spent time with, for example after a dinner at their place. A key part of Swedish politeness.

ex: {Det var länge sedan} vi sågs!
exEn: It's been ages since we last saw each other!
note: sedan is usually said (and often written) sen here. Literally 'it was long ago'.

ex: {Hur gick det} på jobbintervjun?
exEn: How did the job interview go?
note: gick is the past tense of gå. Answer: Det gick bra! (It went well!)

ex: Hej! {Vad gör du} i helgen?
exEn: Hi! What are you doing this weekend?
note: For someone's job, Swedes usually ask: Vad jobbar du med?

en: how do you say … in Swedish?
alt: how do you say in Swedish
how do you say it in Swedish
how do you say that in Swedish
ex: {Hur säger man} ”spoon” på svenska?
exEn: How do you say "spoon" in Swedish?
note: man = one, people in general. Also common: Vad heter … på svenska?

ex: Ursäkta, {vad betyder} det här ordet?
exEn: Excuse me, what does this word mean?
note: betyda = to mean. Vad menar du? = What do you mean (by that)?

ex: Förlåt, jag hörde inte. {Kan du upprepa det}?
exEn: Sorry, I didn't hear. Can you repeat that?
note: More casual: Kan du säga det igen?

ex: {Ta det lugnt}, vi har gott om tid.
exEn: Take it easy, we have plenty of time.
note: Also a casual goodbye: Hej då, ta det lugnt!

ex: {Skynda dig}, bussen går om två minuter!
exEn: Hurry up, the bus leaves in two minutes!
note: sk before y is the sj-sound. To several people: Skynda er!

ex: {Akta dig}, golvet är halt!
exEn: Watch out, the floor is slippery!
note: Akta dig för hunden! = Watch out for the dog! To several people: Akta er!

ex: {Vänta lite}, jag ska bara hämta jackan.
exEn: Wait a moment, I'm just going to get my jacket.
note: More formal: Ett ögonblick! (One moment!)
